sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Indian PhD thesis on the Kaikadi language exists in Shodhganga: the 22 hits are sociology (e.g. Athawale 2023 'Sedentarization of de-notified tribes: the Kaikadis of Maharashtra'; Jadhav 2017; Kolekar 2017), education, law and Dalit-literature theses.
Nothing; only classification, speaker count (25,870 in 2011 census) and IPA of the name; single reference (Census of India 2011).

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (chief ed.) 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Entries 'Yerukula' (pp. 379-385) and 'Yerukula Language' (pp. 385-389).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Kaikadi is named only as 'a Maratha term for Yerukula' (p. 380); the 'Yerukula Language' article's Phonology (p. 386) says there are 31 segmental phonemes plus phonemic nasalisation of vowels (following Varma 1978) and lists vowels/consonants; the words stress/accent do not occur in the article. Ethnographic otherwise; not a Kaikadi description.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages, 'Kaikadi' pp. 333-347 (sketch pp. 333-335; specimens pp. 336-347; Standard Words and Phrases from Sholapur pp. 646ff.). Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3254.1 F; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 5.40; a Harvard library, call number Ud 0010
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Pronunciation' paragraph (pp. 333-334) covers only: long and short vowels commonly interchanged (vandu/vāndu 'he came'), ō~ū interchange (appō/appū), palatals pronounced ts/dz as in Telugu, h corresponding to Tamil p (hō 'go'), final l dropped as in Korava. No accent or stress remark anywhere in the sketch, the specimens, or the Burgandi section (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress over the whole section = zero hits; pages 333-334 checked on the images). Confirms the earlier scan classification.
